unit.title: Angles and Constructions
unit.blurb: Angles at a point, angles on a straight line, vertically opposite angles, angles in a triangle and quadrilateral, and accurate drawing of lines and quadrilaterals.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Know that angles at a point add up to 360° and use this to find missing angles.

O2.t: Recognise angles on a straight line, vertically opposite angles and the angles of a triangle, and find missing angles.

O3.t: Draw parallel and perpendicular lines and construct quadrilaterals accurately with a ruler and protractor.

p: A round pizza is cut from the centre into slices. Three slices have angles **95°, 120° and 80°** at the centre. The last slice is what is left.
What angle does the last slice make at the centre? Try it before you read on.
Angles on a straight line add up to **180°** – half a turn.

p: A full turn is **360°**. So the angles around a point always add up to **360°**.
Pizza: 95 + 120 + 80 = 295, so the last slice is 360 − 295 = **65°**.
Draw a diagonal in any quadrilateral: it splits into **two triangles**. Each triangle's angles add up to 180°, so the angles of a quadrilateral add up to **2 × 180° = 360°**.

p: When two straight lines **intersect** (cross), they make four angles. The angles opposite each other are **equal**. They are called **vertically opposite angles**.
p2: Why? a + b = 180° (straight line) and b + c = 180° (straight line), so a = c. In the same way, b = d.

p: Lines that meet at **90°** are **perpendicular**: all four angles are right angles.
**Parallel** lines never meet; they are marked with arrows. A line crossing them is a **transversal**. It makes eight angles, in two matching groups of four.
p2: **Corresponding angles** (in the same position at each crossing, like an F shape) are equal.
**Alternate angles** (on opposite sides of the transversal, between the parallel lines, like a Z shape) are equal.

captions: Open a pair of scissors.
The two blades cross, and they make 4 angles.
Suppose you open the scissors so that one angle is 40 degrees.
What is the angle next to it?
Pause the video and work it out.
The 40 degree angle and the angle next to it sit on a straight line.
So together they make 180 degrees.
180 minus 40 is 140.
The angle next to it is 140 degrees.
And here is the surprise.
The other two angles are 40 and 140 again.
Let's see why.
Remember two facts.
Angles on a straight line add up to 180 degrees.
And the angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees.
If two angles are 55 and 75, the third is 180 minus 130, which is 50 degrees.
When two straight lines cross, we say they intersect.
They make 4 angles.
Call them a, b, c and d.
The angles opposite each other are equal.
They are called vertically opposite angles.
So a equals c, and b equals d.
Why?
a and b make a straight line, so a plus b is 180.
b and c also make a straight line, so b plus c is 180.
That means a and c must be equal.
Your turn.
Two lines cross, and one angle is 101 degrees.
What is the angle next to it?
Pause the video and try it.
Angles next to each other on a straight line add up to 180.
180 minus 101 is 79 degrees.
Lines that meet at 90 degrees are called perpendicular.
All 4 angles are right angles.
Parallel lines never meet.
On a diagram, they are marked with arrows.
A line that crosses parallel lines is called a transversal.
It makes 8 angles, but there are only 2 different sizes.
Corresponding angles are in matching positions, and they are equal.
Alternate angles are on opposite sides of the transversal, between the parallel lines, and they are equal too.
Here is the method.
Step 1: mark the angles you know on the diagram.
Step 2: use these facts.
Vertically opposite angles are equal.
A straight line is 180.
Around a point is 360.
Step 3: with parallel lines, corresponding angles and alternate angles are equal.
Step 4: write the reason next to each answer.
Two lines intersect.
One angle is 118 degrees.
Find the other three.
The angle vertically opposite is equal, so it is 118 degrees.
The angle next to it is on a straight line.
180 minus 118 is 62 degrees.
And the last angle is vertically opposite that one, so it is 62 degrees as well.
Two vertically opposite angles are 3 x plus 10, and 70 degrees.
Find x.
Vertically opposite angles are equal.
So 3 x plus 10 equals 70.
Subtract 10.
3 x equals 60.
Divide by 3.
x equals 20.
Your turn.
Two vertically opposite angles are 2 y, and 80 degrees.
What is y?
Pause and work it out.
They are equal, so 2 y equals 80.
Divide by 2.
y equals 40.
A transversal crosses two parallel lines.
One angle is 48 degrees.
The alternate angle is equal.
So it is also 48 degrees.
The angle on a straight line with it is 180 minus 48, which is 132 degrees.
Two lines cross.
One angle is 35 degrees.
Mia wants the angle vertically opposite it.
Which line is wrong?
Line 1 is wrong.
Vertically opposite angles are equal.
It is the angles next to each other that add up to 180.
So the vertically opposite angle is 35 degrees.
Railway tracks are a famous example of parallel lines.
On most of the world's railways, the two rails are exactly 1,435 millimetres apart.
If the rails were not parallel, the gap would change, and the train would come off the track.
The wooden sleepers under the rails cross them at right angles.
They are perpendicular to the rails.
One last question.
Between two parallel lines, an angle is 57 degrees.
What is its alternate angle?
Pause the video and answer.
Alternate angles are equal.
So the alternate angle is 57 degrees.
To remember: vertically opposite angles are equal.
Angles on a straight line add up to 180 degrees.
Around a point, 360.
Perpendicular lines meet at 90 degrees.
With parallel lines, corresponding angles and alternate angles are equal.

p: To draw a line **perpendicular** to line AB through point P: put one edge of a set square along AB and slide it until the other edge reaches P, then draw. With a protractor: centre on P, 90° mark along the line, draw along the 90° line.
To draw a line **parallel** to AB through P: draw a perpendicular at two places, measure the same distance on each, and join the points – or slide a set square along a ruler.
To draw a quadrilateral from its measurements, draw **one side first**, then use a protractor for each angle and a ruler for each length.

lesson.t: How do I draw a quadrilateral accurately?

Step 3: Measure each angle at the ends with a protractor and draw the next sides to the right length.
Step 4: Join up; check lengths (to 1 mm) and angles (to 1°) and label everything.

No protractor needed.

What is true about the angles of a kite?
Pause the video and choose.
A kite has one pair of equal opposite angles.
It also has two pairs of equal sides next to each other.
To remember: perpendicular lines meet at 90 degrees, and parallel lines never meet.
Use a set square or a protractor for perpendicular lines, and a sliding set square for parallel lines.
To draw a quadrilateral: sketch, draw one side, measure the angles, mark the lengths.
Check with what you know: equal diagonals, equal opposite angles, and neighbours that add up to 180.
